sources.citation: Stark, Tammy Elizabeth. 2018. Caribbean Northern Arawak person marking and alignment: a comparative and diachronic analysis. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley.
sources.note: No phonology content. Sec. 1.2: 'a single wordlist containing 17 items for Shebayo (Aikhenvald, 1999)'; fn. 5: Shebayo data (16 items, 3% lexical coverage) omitted from the final phylogenetic analysis.

sources.citation: Boomert, Arie. 2016. The Indigenous Peoples of Trinidad and Tobago from the First Settlers until Today. Leiden: Sidestone Press. 218 pp.
sources.note: Ethnohistorical monograph; mentions the 1598 wordlists but gives no linguistic material or analysis; nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center.
sources.note: Location/source line plus 5-6 wordlist items (wa-kewüri 'head', nu-yeri 'tooth', wa-daköli 'eye', tuna? etc.) in a comparative table; no phonological or prosodic statement.

sources.citation: Taylor, Douglas. 1957. Languages and Ghost-Languages of the West Indies: A Postscript. International Journal of American Linguistics 23(2): 114-119.
sources.note: Re-edition of the de Laet list in the recorder's spelling (heja, hamma, wackewijrrij, wackenoey, noeyerri, wassi, darrymaily, wadacoely, watabaye, wackehyrry, ataly, hoerapallii, hewerry, kyrtzyrre, wecoelije) with glosses and cognates; no accent marks, no remark on pronunciation or prosody.

sources.citation: Taylor, Douglas. 1956. Languages and Ghost-Languages of the West Indies. International Journal of American Linguistics 22(2): 180-183.
sources.note: No phonology content for Shebayo. p. 182: 'What little is known of the languages of Trinidad appears to be contained in de Laet's short lists, collected in Trinidad in 1598, of Lokono.., Jaoi.., and Shebayo.. These lists contain only the words for father, mother, head, ear, eye, nose, mouth, teeth, leg, feet, tree, bow, arrows, moon and sun, but some of them include a pronominal prefix of the first person'. (The only stress remark in the note concerns Island Carib vs Black Carib, not Shebayo.)

sources.citation: Taylor, Douglas. 1951. Review of C. H. de Goeje, Nouvel examen des langues des Antilles.. (JSA 31, 1939). International Journal of American Linguistics 17(4): 257-259. doi:10.1086/464137
sources.note: Only: the work contains 'two brief word-lists of Shebayo and Guayana respectively'; the review's phonological discussion concerns Island Carib. No Shebayo phonology.

sources.citation: de Goeje, C. H. 1940. Nouvel examen des langues des Antilles. Errata. Journal de la Societe des Americanistes 32(2): 296-297.
sources.note: Errata table (page/line/read-for); the scanned first page lists orthographic corrections to pp. 5-20 (Taino/Island Carib sections) and a Taylor 1938 reference; nothing on pronunciation or prosody; second page not rendered in Persee's inline scanned.

sources.citation: de Goeje, C. H. 1939. Nouvel examen des langues des Antilles avec notes sur les langues arawak-maipure et caribes et vocabulaires shebayo et guayana (Guyane). Journal de la Société des Américanistes 31(1): 1-120 (Shebayo: pp. 4-5, 117-118). doi:10.3406/jsa.1939.1984
sources.note: Nothing. pp. 4-5: de Laet gives a short Shebayo vocabulary; analysis places it in Arawak-Maipure but distinct from Aruan, Palikur, Lokono. pp. 117-118: the 15 words re-edited with comparanda; only structural remark is 'La syllabe initiale wa- est probablement le préfixe personnel indiquant la 1re pers. du plur; la syllabe finale -ly, -ri est peut-être suffixe.'

sources.citation: de Goeje, C. H. 1939. Nouvel examen des langues des Antilles. JSA 31(1): 1-120 — publisher PDF.
sources.note: Text already read in full via Persée's open per-page scanned; the page-image PDF (docAsPDF) is behind an altcha proof-of-work gate and was not. Only needed if a facsimile of pp. 117-118 is wanted.

sources.citation: de Laet, Joannes. 1633. Novus orbis seu Descriptionis Indiae Occidentalis libri XVIII. Lugduni Batavorum: apud Elzevirios. Lib. XVII, cap. XII 'De barbarorum horum idiomate, praesertim Yaiorum', p. 642.
sources.note: Nothing. The whole Shebayo record is a 13-item column 'Shebayis' (Heja, Hamma, Wackewijrrij, Wackenoely, Noeyerii, Wassibaly, Darrymaily, Wadacoely, Watabaye, Wackehyrry, Ataly, Hoerapallii, Hewerry) plus 'Shebaioi Kyrtryrre' (moon) and 'She: Wecoelije' (sun); no accents, no remarks on pronunciation.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page sheb1234 Shebayo (refs: de Laet 1633 pp. 642-643; Ramirez 2020 p. 648; comment 'attested by a very short wordlist', classified Unclassified Wapishanan).
Native Languages of the Americas (website). n.d. 'Shebayo Words (Shebaye)' -- vocabulary page compiling ~20 Shebayo words from de Laet (1633) and Loukotka (1968).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content: 'Shebayo has long been extinct, so our only records of the language are wordlists recorded in the 17th and 18th century'; a comparative word table without accent marks or any pronunciation/prosody remark (wordlist-only data, second-hand).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Shebayo language' (cites de Laet 1633, de Goeje 1939, Taylor 1977, Aikhenvald 1999; reproduces the ~15-word list).

de Laet, Joannes. 1630. Beschrijvinghe van West-Indien (Nieuwe Wereldt ofte Beschrijvinghe van West-Indien, 2nd Dutch ed.). Leyden: Elzevier. [Guiana chapters, pp. 568-572; DBNL text edition laet004besc02]
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnographic-geographic text: location of the Shebaios (p. 568), 'Yaos, Sappaios, Arwaccas, Paragotos' fled from Trinidad or the Orinoco (p. 570), body paint 'Annoti' named as a Yao and Shebayo word (p. 571). No word list, no remark on speech or pronunciation.
